title: Pseudo-Distributions: Thermodynamic Geometry and an Empirical Application
authors: Negin Bayrami, Hosein Mohammadzadeh, Hamzeh Agahi, Hossein Mehri-Dehnavi, Zahra Ebadi
abstract: We develop a consistent pseudo-analytic framework based on $g$-calculus for constructing deformed statistical distributions. By mapping standard algebraic operations through a monotone generator function, we systematically derive the associated pseudo-logarithmic and pseudo-exponential structures. Applying this formalism, we introduce a new family of pseudo-distributions that generalizes nonextensive statistical mechanics at both the probability density and cumulative distribution levels, recovering classical and standard nonextensive statistics as limiting cases. We investigate the thermodynamic geometry of the proposed models using the Ruppeiner metric on the equilibrium manifold. A perturbative analysis around the classical limit reveals that, to leading order, the thermodynamic scalar curvature is governed solely by the generator deformation parameter, while the nonextensivity parameter remains decoupled. To evaluate the empirical robustness of the framework, we apply the model to analyze the absolute deviations of daily West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices from their hundred-day moving average. Model comparison based on information criteria demonstrates that the proposed pseudo-distributions provide a superior description of these high-frequency financial fluctuations and their heavy-tailed characteristics compared to standard benchmarks. These results suggest that $g$-calculus offers a flexible and physically grounded mathematical tool for generating deformed statistics and analyzing their geometric properties.
summary: This work introduces a novel pseudo-analytic framework based on g-calculus to generalize statistical distributions beyond standard nonextensive models. It analyzes the thermodynamic geometry associated with these new distributions and demonstrates their superior ability to model heavy-tailed fluctuations observed in real-world financial data like oil prices.
main_problem: The paper develops a pseudo-analytic framework using g-calculus to construct generalized statistical distributions, aiming to systematically extend nonextensive statistical mechanics.
main_result: The proposed pseudo-distributions provide a superior fit for analyzing heavy-tailed fluctuations in financial data (WTI oil prices) and reveal that the thermodynamic scalar curvature is governed by the generator deformation parameter at leading order.
method: Methods include developing g-calculus structures, calculating thermodynamic geometry using the Ruppeiner metric, and performing empirical model comparison using information criteria (AIC/BIC).
model_or_system: The theoretical framework applies to general statistical ensembles, tested both by analyzing ideal gas thermodynamics in D dimensions and empirically by fitting absolute deviations of WTI crude oil prices.
key_observables: Thermodynamic scalar curvature ($R$), goodness-of-fit metrics (AIC/BIC), and the distribution function itself.
important_parameters: Generator deformation parameter ($\alpha$), nonextensivity parameter ($q$), and the fugacity parameter ($z$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes $g$-calculus is applicable via a monotone generator function, and analyses often rely on perturbative expansions around classical limits.
figures_summary: Figure 4 shows WTI oil price fluctuations vs. moving average; Figure 5 plots the fitted pseudo-nonextensive Tsallis distribution to the absolute deviation of WTI prices from its moving average.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing g-calculus, generalizing distributions at PDF/CDF levels, investigating thermodynamic geometry via curvature calculations, and concluding with empirical applications to financial time series data.
why_interesting: While the application is finance, the underlying mathematical tools—generalized entropy frameworks and geometric analysis of equilibrium states—are highly relevant for characterizing complex, non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body quantum systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

Panel (a) corresponds to the pseudo-generalized exponential model obtained directly from the PDF, while panel (b) represents the model constructed by pseudo-generalizing the CDF. In both cases, α < 1 leads to positive curvature, α > 1 results in negative curvature, and the classical exponential limit α = 1 yields vanishing curvature.
